explanation: The December 12, 2012 document contains highly substantive policy content that straddles the break date: it announced the replacement of the expiring Maturity Extension Program with $45 billion/month in outright Treasury purchases (a new, open-ended QE component), and critically introduced explicit state-based forward guidance thresholds (6.5% unemployment, 2.5% inflation) replacing the prior calendar-based guidance—a major framework shift. These announcements on December 12 would plausibly drive a structural break in financial market data around year-end 2012.
